title: Rehearsal Playground — interactive prompt rehearsal lab
body:
Context / problem:

I keep getting requests from product and SEs for a tool that makes it easy to iterate on prompt UX while understanding real downstream costs and latency tradeoffs. The quick experiments folks do in the web prompt playground don’t capture multi-turn behaviour, cache effects, or what a rollout will actually cost at scale. We need something between a throwaway scratchpad and a full eval harness: fast, reproducible, and surfaced in the Console and SDK.

Idea (high level): Rehearsal Playground = an interactive lab where you “rehearse” sequences of interactions against realistic serving profiles. Key features:
- Multi-turn recording & replay: record a conversation (from local dev or from staged traffic) and replay it against different model variants, batching configs, and caching policies.
- Mock infra knobs: simulate batch sizes, KV cache hit rates, quantization (fp16/8-bit), and region routing to see latency/cost deltas.
- Cost/latency estimation: per-play and aggregated estimates showing token counts, inferred GPU-seconds, and an expected cost delta compared to baseline.
- Failure mode toggles: inject slow nodes, drop connections, or force model fallbacks to see graceful-degradation UX.
- Snapshot diffs and annotations: side-by-side response diffs with inline notes and scorecards (quality, hallucination flags, safety hits).
- Exportable runs: save a rehearsal as JSON for CI evals or as a terse script to run against Dedicated instances.

Why this matters:
- Helps PMs and SEs make informed model choices before rolling out to production.
- Encourages safer, cheaper rollouts by making tradeoffs explicit early.
- Reduces wasted infra costs from naive A/Bs because teams can pre-simulate expected load/cost.

User stories (rough):
1) As an SE helping an enterprise customer, I want to replay the customer’s 20-step onboarding chat against two model variants and see expected cost & latency so we can recommend a SKU.
2) As a PM designing a lower-cost tier, I want to test synthetic 10k-user load by replaying a canonical flow under a higher batching policy to estimate savings.
3) As a developer, I want to annotate responses where safety heuristics differ between models so the content team can review the tradeoffs.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI: simple playground page in Console that can import conversation JSON (or paste), select up to 3 model variants/config presets, and run a rehearsal.
- Backend: sample runner that executes replay logic against our hosted models and returns tokenized traces + timing breakdown.
- Reports: per-rehearsal cost/latency summary + side-by-side response diff view.
- Persistence: ability to save runs to account-level storage and share link with collaborators.

Non-goals for MVP:
- Real traffic capture (we'll accept manually uploaded transcripts or staged traffic import later).
- Full CI integration (export only, CI hooking comes next quarter).

Implementation sketches / signals:
- Rehearsal runner sits in Redwood Console infra but uses same inference routing stack; it should support running against hosted and dedicated endpoints via an internal test token.
- To keep cost low, we can run with throttled concurrency and synthetic arrival times (playback speed control).
- Cache modelling: naive approach first — allow toggling cache-hit-rate as a param that adjusts token cost/latency using offline profiling numbers. Later we can enable actual KV reuse if replay runs on a warm endpoint.
- Batching simulation: two modes — (1) simulated batching using arrival-time model to compute expected batch sizes and latency impacts, and (2) real batching by actually firing requests with controlled inter-arrival times to a test endpoint (more accurate but costlier).

Metrics to surface:
- Token counts (input/outputs), tokens-per-second, estimated GPU-seconds, estimated $ cost (breakdown by model and batching/caching assumptions), median/95/99 latency, safety flags count, and quality deltas (BLEU-like or custom scorer).

UI notes / quick wire text:
- Left panel: conversation import / small editor (paste JSON, upload .ndjson, or record via devtools).
- Top controls: select models (dropdown), toggle presets (low-latency, low-cost, balanced), set cache-hit %, set replay speed, toggle failure scenarios.
- Main: side-by-side columns for model A / model B (or A/B/C), each with a time-aligned transcript, token and latency badges on each turn, and inline right-side diff/comment toolbar.
- Bottom: summary tiles (cost, latency, safety). Export button -> JSON / CI script.

Open questions / risks: 
- Data security: if customers upload real transcripts, need clear guidance + opt-in retention policy. Default: transient storage (30 days max), optional encrypted buckets for enterprise.
- Pricing signals: if we expose cost estimates, need to ensure they don’t mislead (we should show assumptions explicitly).
- Cost of running rehearsals: long replays or large-scale simulated loads could be expensive; limit per-run quotas or charge credits.
- Dedicated/Private support: how to allow a customer to run rehearsals against their private deployment without exposing control-plane tokens? Possible approach: Rehearsal exports a script the customer runs in their VPC which writes back summarized metrics.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Draft a short proto UI mock (low-fi) for Console team — assign to Maya for initial sketch (due 2025-08-22).
- Engineering spike: Kai to implement a replay runner prototype that can call 2 model variants and produce timing traces (target: 2 weeks).
- Security check: loop in Security for retention and acceptable data handling (ask for guidance on default TTL and encryption).
- Define a small set of canonical flows (support + onboarding + search-assist) for internal benchmarking.

Notes to self (random):
- Could be neat to couple with Optimize recommendations: after a rehearsal, show suggested batching/quantization that would hit a target cost delta.
- Long term: make rehearsal runs part of rollout gates (must pass quality/cost checks before canary).
- Keep it as a developer-first tool — power users should be able to script runs via SDK.

End of brainstorm.  

Quick log: 2025-08-15 morning — sketched while pairing with SE lead on a customer call. 2025-09-02 — refined user stories and added export/priv-deploy notes based on internal feedback.
